description: OpenAPI 3.1 path-operation coverage and exhaustive source-artifact disposition evidence.

scenarios.description: A supported path operation remains callable while every request-media declaration and webhook dependency receives its own disposition; the object-schema custom media selects no carriage lane [CO31-05].

A parameter/body-property collision is preserved because the synthesized flat contract maps through inputTransform to disjoint parameters and body envelope members, so both media alternatives remain represented [CO31-03].
A required body property colliding with a parameter remains independently callable because synthesis maps its flat contract through inputTransform to disjoint envelope members [CO31-03].
An absolute sole server makes an ordinary path operation directly invocable without a server-selection prerequisite.
A content-form parameter outside the specification's JSON and text carriage is excluded at synthesis instead of producing an operation that can never faithfully send the declared value.
A document-level custom schema dialect excludes the whole source; neither schema-free operations nor per-schema overrides can reopen the source-scope exclusion.
OAS 3.1 schema-omitted raw bytes and schema-declared encoded text are both represented without collapsing their distinct wire carriage.
A range-only request body remains a represented protocol-blind operation while coverage records the concrete request-media choice required for invocation.
A mixed exact-plus-range request has no target-wide media requirement, while the represented range alternative records the concrete choice it needs.
An optional range-only body has no target-wide requirement because bodyless invocation is available, while its represented range alternative still requires concrete request media.

A declaration-complex exact JSON request remains fully represented: synthesis owns the flat operation contract and emits inputTransform to the envelope's one body value; the binding has no declaration-complex correspondence trigger [CO31-03].
A part schema declaring one non-null anyOf branch beside a null branch collapses to that branch's carriage and is represented, while a choice with more than one non-null branch keeps its exclusion.

file.description: The file to process; JSON null elides the part.

scenarios.description: The string-carriage lane needs both halves of a derived scope: a governing schema that resolves to type string, and a media type that is character data. A concrete non-JSON, non-form declaration meeting both is represented -- text/plain, text/csv, and XML alike -- while the same media types declared with an object schema select no lane, because no lane builds a document from an object model. A media type whose registration establishes no character encoding has no defined string-to-octets mapping, so a string-typed binary declaration keeps the byte boundary and is an excluded alternative; under OAS 3.1 format binary carries no assertion force, so that declaration resolves to a bare type string and is decided entirely by its media type. A schema that asserts nothing is the same declaration as an omitted schema and takes the artifact-authorized byte lane.

A self-recursive component is reached from the request body only through a property the OAS declares readOnly, and from the response body directly. Request projection removes the property, so the emitted input contract must not publish a definition for a component no request instance can contain, while the output contract keeps the same component as its own recursive definition. Both boundaries stay realizable and the operation is fully represented.

JSON Schema 2020-12 defines an array-valued type as a union, so a form part typed ["string", "null"] declares exactly what the collapsing anyOf spelling declares and takes the same carriage: the part is represented, its sibling keywords still apply, and a supplied JSON null elides the optional part. A part typed ["string", "object"] declares two non-null alternatives, leaves no single faithful form carriage, and is an excluded alternative -- the same answer a choice with more than one non-null branch gets. Under the OAS 3.0 line, whose Schema Object requires type to be a string and does not support multiple types via an array, the same union spelling is not a union declaration and its multipart alternative is excluded there too.

A reference cycle closes through a schema position the artifact addresses but does not declare under components.schemas: `#/components/schemas/Wrapper/properties/inner` references itself. The cycle is a cycle wherever it closes, so the emitted operation schema must cut it at the addressed position and stay self-contained; emitting the artifact-space reference into the OBI would publish a reference that does not resolve in the emitted document (OBI-D-16). The operation is realizable and fully represented.

Whether a declared server URL denotes a target address at all decides whether the server configuration point is a runtime prerequisite of the represented target. A sole entry selects itself and, when it resolves, requires nothing. A sole entry whose URL template variable has no Server Variable Object remains represented but requires configuration.server, because a complete configured URL can discharge the invocation; a declared variable's default reduces normally. A hostless HTTP authority remains the same configurable target-base prerequisite, and a multi-entry list requires selection. In contrast, a Server URL containing a query is upstream-invalid and its owning target is accounted invalid rather than excluded. Neither answer may be decided by a host language's URL parser.

OAS 3.1.1 tabulates the Encoding Object default contentType for a part whose `type` is absent as application/octet-stream, in the first row of that field's own table. The part is thereby routed to octets by the authority itself, and openbindings.openapi-3.1@1 carries them with the canonical Base64 boundary it already defines for its byte lanes, so a multipart alternative carrying such a part is represented. This scenario pinned the opposite until 2026-08-20 — the alternative excluded and the sole-candidate target excluded with it — on the ground that no JSON-to-octet part boundary existed; it did, and the revision-is-not-a-roadmap ruling directed the gap filled rather than deferred. uploadAvatar is represented on its sole alternative, createNote on both of its, and createLabel, whose part declares `type: string`, is unaffected. OAS 3.1.2 carries the same row verbatim and takes the same dispositions.

OAS 3.1.0 states the same answer as 3.1.1 for a part whose `type` is absent, by a different sentence: its Encoding Object contentType enumeration closes with a total catch-all — "for object - application/json; for array - the default is defined based on the inner type; for all other cases the default is application/octet-stream" — whose complement includes a declaration carrying no type at all. The part is thereby routed to octets by the authority itself, and openbindings.openapi-3.1@1 carries them with the canonical Base64 boundary it already defines for its byte lanes, so a multipart alternative carrying such a part is represented. This scenario pinned the opposite until 2026-08-20 — the alternative excluded and the sole-candidate target excluded with it — on the ground that no JSON-to-octet part boundary existed; it did, and the revision-is-not-a-roadmap ruling directed the gap filled rather than deferred. The dispositions are therefore the 3.1.1 ones, and this scenario exists because that ground is an implied answer rather than a tabulated row.

openbindings.openapi-3.1@1 section 6 composes the value AT the referenced JSON Pointer together with that value's transitive closure of references, and nothing else. A dangling reference in a component the pointer never reaches is outside that closure, so the referencing artifact resolves and its operation is represented. A whole-file composer refuses the same artifact.

source.content:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./library.yaml#/components/schemas/Used"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

scenarios.description: The twin of the scenario above, differing only in which component carries the dangling reference. Reachable from the referenced pointer and unresolvable there, it makes the referencing artifact unresolvable, and the whole source refuses. The pair is what shows the pointer-scoped rule narrowed composition rather than merely widening acceptance.

The artifact resolves. No assertion pins the emitted body value, because the operation property that would carry it is named by the synthesizer rather than by the artifact.

scenarios.description: Two references compose two elements of the same sequence and the defective element between them is composed by neither. Index identity has to survive that: allOf/2 must still denote the third element, so no index may be renumbered when one is left out. The two assertions are what distinguish surviving indices from a silently compacted sequence, which the operation set alone cannot see.

scenarios.description: Every accepted OAS 3.1 edition keys the application/octet-stream part default on a DECLARED string carrying `contentEncoding` — 3.1.0 as "a `type: string` with a `contentEncoding`", 3.1.1 and 3.1.2 as the Encoding Object default table's `string` row with contentEncoding present. On a declared non-string type the keyword is inert: the same table holds `n/a` in the contentEncoding column of the `number, integer, or boolean` and `object` rows, defined by its own note as "the presence or value of contentEncoding is irrelevant", and JSON Schema 2020-12 makes the Content vocabulary annotations that "do not function as validation assertions", each conditioned on a string instance. So recordSample and recordProfile keep the text/plain and application/json rows and are represented; uploadAvatar takes the encoded-string row and is represented; and createNote's part, which declares no `type` at all, reaches the `type`-absent row's application/octet-stream and rides the canonical Base64 boundary this specification already defines for its byte lanes, so that alternative and its sole-candidate target are represented too — the same disposition OAPI31-SS-23 pins for its `/avatars` target. The keyword-inertness this scenario exists to pin is therefore visible in the content types, not in an exclusion.

scenarios.description: The twin of the scenario above on a byte-identical artifact apart from the declared edition. No 3.1 edition incorporates JSON Reference; the 3.1 Schema Object is a superset of JSON Schema 2020-12, whose section 8.2.3.1 carries the authors' note that other keywords can appear alongside "$ref" in the same schema object. The node keeps its own members, the token names one of them, and the composed value is the sibling. The pair is what shows the rule is the incorporated authority's and splits by edition line rather than being one averaged convention.

scenarios.description: The retention consequence of OAPI31-SS-32's reading, as a defect. Because the composed value is the sibling, the $ref the fragment walked past is composed by nothing, and section 6's reference scope — the value at the pointer plus that value's own transitive closure, and nothing else — puts its target outside the artifact. A dangling target there is a defect outside the closure, which does not make the referencing artifact unresolvable. Its OAPI30-SS-33 twin is the same artifact on the other edition line, where the same reference IS composed and the same defect refuses.

scenarios.description: The 3.1 half of an edition-scoped pair whose member bytes are identical to OAPI30-SS-38's. A 3.1 type array contributes every listed type to the resolved set and is not the single-non-null-branch choice procedure used for anyOf/oneOf. Therefore neither {"type":["object","null"]} nor {"type":["object","string"]} declares only a compound kind, and the declaration-keyed compound-member exclusion reaches neither operation.

The ACCOUNTING half of section 9.2's normalized-collision confinement. Two content-map keys denoting one parsed media identity are a collision that confines to that identity: each colliding key is an accounted `excluded` alternative under the ordinary OAPI31-P-03 media-exclusion reason, while the map's non-colliding sibling stays represented and the required-body operation survives on it. Before confinement the whole candidate set was unresolvable and the operation disappeared.

The acceptance floor's Schema Object verdict on the 3.1 line is the GOVERNING DIALECT'S, not a keyword list of ours. Absent `jsonSchemaDialect` -- and this document sets none -- every accepted 3.1 edition says in the same words that "the OAS dialect schema id MUST be used for these Schema Objects", and that dialect (https://spec.openapis.org/oas/3.1/dialect/base) composes the ROOT JSON Schema 2020-12 meta-schema. Two of its constraints are unreachable by anyone enumerating keywords from the vocabulary texts. `$recursiveAnchor` appears ZERO times in either pinned 2020-12 draft, yet the root meta-schema deliberately re-declares it as an anchor STRING -- "This meta-schema also defines keywords that have appeared in previous drafts in order to prevent incompatible extensions as they remain in common use" -- so a boolean fails a guard no vocabulary states. And `required` reaches `uniqueItems` through `$defs/stringArray`, so a DUPLICATED entry is invalid even though the array is an array. Each defect confines to the smallest unit that owns it, per Section 3's floor: `describeFilter` and `listContainers` lose their targets and every other operation is delivered. The three operations beside them are the negative controls that make the delegation's shape visible rather than its outcome: a STRING-valued `$recursiveAnchor` is legal (the meta-schema types the keyword, it does not ban it), `$recursiveRef: "#"` is legal (re-declared as a URI reference, which `#` satisfies), and `nullable`, a misspelled `min_items` and an arbitrary vendor keyword are legal annotations under core Section 4.3.1 and the edition's own "or entirely arbitrary properties". A conformant processor that refused any of those three would be narrowing what the authority admits. `searchFilters` carries the other measured consequence of the same confinement: its REQUIRED request body declares exactly one media alternative, that alternative is the invalid unit, and so the target is excluded under OAPI31-P-03's unresolvable-request-body rule rather than becoming an invalid target itself -- the ladder confining at the alternative and the operation losing its target for a different, already-stated reason.
A reusable Callback Object resolves into a targetless dependency at its parent declaration slot while retaining the callback operation's authored request and response contracts [OAPI31-S-01].

The synthesis face of §8.2's whole-row test, which the chain-trace program restated from a per-CELL test to a per-ROW one. The test decides whether a target is published at all, so the three operations here are the discrimination itself. spaceExplode carries spaceDelimited with explode true, whose Style Examples row is n/a in ALL FOUR of its columns — undefined, string, array, object — so no value it could ever be supplied has a defined expansion and its TARGET is excluded before any caller value exists; a parameter has no sibling alternative to fall back to, so the unit owning the defect is the operation. deepDefaulted is the instance §8.2 names by name: an omitted explode on deepObject computes to false, whose row the edition itself calls undefined, so the defaulting alone excludes it. spaceCollapsed is the control the restatement is for: the same style with explode false is a MIXED row — n/a for undefined and string, real bytes for array and object — and under the superseded per-cell reading its n/a undefined cell would have excluded it too. It stays represented, and its published input is what the assertion pins. OAPI31-PS-148, -149 and -150 are the invocation-side halves of the same three cells. The reasonCode spelling recorded a disagreement until 2026-08-31: openbindings-go emitted openapi.parameter_content_excluded here because its serialization-validity check ran inside its content-parameter check and inherited that bucket's code and message — false evidence, since these parameters declare no content — while openbindings-ts ran the same check at its own site as openapi.parameter_serialization_excluded, which truthfully names the check that fires. The convergence keeps the TS spelling: the interface-synthesizer contract requires a stable family-namespaced reason code, no binding-specification rule states one, and the spelling that names its own evidence wins over the one that borrowed a neighbouring bucket's. The composite-MEMBER case keeps its distinct shared spelling openapi.parameter_style_expansion_excluded in both engines.

A request-body Schema Object whose `allOf` branches intersect emptily is a WELL-FORMED upstream declaration that admits no instance, and the JSON-lane position it governs is accounted `represented` with `fullyRepresented: true`. The governing dialect's validity condition for `allOf` is structural only — a non-empty array whose elements are valid schemas — and neither that dialect nor any accepted OAS edition gives satisfiability any role, so nothing about `allOf: [{type: string}, {type: object}]` is upstream-invalid; Core OBI-D-17 says the same from the other side, requiring no proof of satisfiability for a schema to be well-formed. §12.2 admits `invalid` only where the declaration is upstream-invalid, and §3.2 keeps `invalid` and `excluded` apart on exactly that line, so this position is neither: the emitted OBI carries the declaration as written, nothing is projected away, and coverage stays fully represented. The `application/json` lane is selected by media type rather than by the resolved declaration, which is why no admission test gates this position; the intersecting sibling is the control that keeps the scenario about the empty intersection rather than about `allOf`. Where the resolved declaration DOES select carriage — the character-data and raw-octet lanes, a multipart part, a urlencoded property — §9.1's stated no-admissible-candidate rule excludes the alternative instead, which is a different rule with a different status and is not asserted here.

A REQUIRED text/plain body whose Schema Object `allOf` branches intersect emptily is a WELL-FORMED declaration that admits no instance, and on the character-data lane that fact selects no carriage: Section 9.2 admits a character-data selection only for a resolved declaration that admits `string` as its sole non-null type, an empty intersection admits none, so the candidate is inadmissible and Section 9.1's rule for a body-emitting invocation with no admissible candidate applies. With text/plain as the ONLY declared request media and the body required, no invocable form remains, and the target is excluded: one entry, on the target, and the operation is not synthesized. This is the character-data half of OAPI31-SS-47's JSON-lane cell, where the same declaration is because that lane is selected by media type alone and consults no resolved declaration. The control operation carries an ordinary on the same lane and is represented with its alternative. This scenario exists because the two reference engines agreed the target is excluded and disagreed on the reason code, and the corpus was silent. The 2026-08-15 request-side string-carriage ruling decides it: the character-data lane is selected BY the declaration, so a declaration that does not resolve to string selects no lane at all rather than selecting one and then failing a schema test. That is openapi.unresolvable_request_body — no declared media type selects a request carriage lane — and not openapi.media_schema_mismatch, which names a degenerate combination on a lane the media type DID select (a non-object multipart body, a form property with no single faithful carriage, OAPI30-SS-35). It asserts nothing about a multipart part or a content-form property whose declaration intersects emptily; that accounting is not pinned here.

A content-form property or multipart part whose Schema Object `allOf` branches intersect emptily is a WELL-FORMED declaration that admits no instance, and it is an UNREACHABLE defect under Section 3.2's smallest-owner rule: no value can ever reach it, so it destroys neither its media alternative nor its target, both are accounted represented, and the declaration is carried into the synthesized contract as written. This is the same accounting both content-based lanes already apply to a boolean `false` property, of which the empty intersection is the resolved form; it is NOT the accounting for a property with no single faithful carriage (OAPI30-SS-35), where conforming values exist and the lane cannot carry them, nor the style lane's statically-refused member (OAPI30-SS-36), where every conforming value is refused — here there is no conforming value at all, and exclusion would remove a target on a defect nothing reaches. Three requestBody shapes are pinned so the accounting cannot depend on them: a required multipart body whose only alternative carries the property, the same alternative beside an application/json sibling, and an optional urlencoded body. The invoke half — a value supplied for the property refuses before dispatch at that part, Section 5.2's consequence — is pinned by the companion processor scenario on this line. This scenario exists because the two reference engines disagreed here (one excluded the target, one represented it) while agreeing on the boolean false, and the corpus was silent.

Path-template synthesis preserves the 3.1 authority boundary. A repeated expression is upstream-valid and remains represented, with one effective path Parameter supplying every occurrence; an expression with no corresponding effective path Parameter is upstream-invalid and is accounted invalid rather than excluded (OAPI31-S-01, OAPI31-P-02).
